lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Decision Analysis and Expected Value Capstone
lessonRef.focus: fair decisions and the role of randomness
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: fair decisions and the role of randomness

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A has expected payoff $12, B has $9. Which, and what is ignored?

steps: A has the higher expected value.
Spread and risk tolerance are not captured.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning faces 1–3, 4–5, and 6.
choices: Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.

items.prompt: A game costs $3 to play. It pays $112 with probability 1/7 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $16; the game is favourable to the player
$109; the game is favourable to the player
$13; the game is favourable to the player
$-3; the game is unfavourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $16 and pays out $720 with probability 1/180. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $55 and Option B has expected payoff $24. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option A; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.

items.prompt: A game costs $13 to play. It pays $273 with probability 1/7 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $-13; the game is unfavourable to the player
$39; the game is favourable to the player
$260; the game is favourable to the player
$26; the game is favourable to the player

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $23 and pays out $742 with probability 1/106. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $48 and Option B has expected payoff $50. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
